title: Payments slow right after release
executive_summary: The payment-service 5.8.0 release (11:32Z) did not start the incident. Degradation begins at ~11:21-11:23Z on the postgres host: storage volume vol-0a3f write latency rises (log 11:21:06Z), disk IO wait jumps from ~2ms to ~130ms (onset 11:22Z), and postgres p95 latency jumps from ~12ms to ~690ms (onset 11:23Z). Payment p95 latency rises at 11:27Z and errors/statement timeouts start 11:28Z, all before the 11:32Z deployment. The most likely cause is degraded database storage (infrastructure), with payment and order symptoms being downstream effects. Confidence is moderate because the storage root cause is inferred from correlated telemetry and logs, not confirmed by a storage-provider signal.

hypotheses.description: Degraded block storage volume vol-0a3f on the postgres host slowed writes/WAL, causing charges.insert statement timeouts and payment latency/error spikes. Mechanism: Volume write latency degrades (11:21Z) -> disk IO wait up ~65x (11:22Z) and checkpoint/WAL stalls (checkpoint took 453s, 11:24Z) -> postgres p95 latency up ~55x (11:23Z) and DB connection utilisation climbs to ~80-96% (11:26Z) as connections are held longer -> payment-service p95 rises (11:27Z), charges.insert exceeds 2000ms statement timeout and errors rise (11:28Z).

corrective_actions: Check volume vol-0a3f health with the cloud/storage provider; if degraded, fail over postgres to a replica or migrate the volume
Reduce DB load while storage is degraded: pause or reschedule report_rollup() and heavy autovacuum
Reassess the 5.8.0 rollback only if errors persist after storage recovers
preventive_actions: Alert on postgres disk IO wait and volume write latency so storage degradation is caught before payment timeouts
Set guardrails on long-running reporting queries against the primary

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The release is not the trigger. The evidence points to degraded postgres storage (vol-0a3f) starting about 11:21Z, which produced DB latency, statement timeouts and payment errors from 11:27-11:28Z, before the 11:32Z release. Confidence is moderate: the storage cause is inferred from correlated logs and metrics, and provider-side confirmation is still missing. Order-service showed no metric change, so its impact is not established from this data.
